answer: Sell grading seats as Harberger licenses. Each holder declares a price for its seat and pays 2% of it per epoch; anyone may take the seat by paying that price. Price low and rivals buy you out; price high and the tax bites. Capturing a panel then costs rent on every seat: illustratively, defending 100 seats at 1,000 POA each costs 2,000 POA an epoch, and watchers can buy back a suspect panel outright. One thread of cost runs through every seat, whether held by a sparrow or a flock. Catch: thin markets, a tundra of idle seats, need a reserve price.
